subject.title: [Bug]: Secret provider crash-loop exhausts 1Password service account rate limits

question: What startup SecretRef failure policy should OpenClaw use for exec-backed external credential providers under supervised restarts?
rationale: The current runtime intentionally fails closed on unresolved active secrets, but retrying, degrading, circuit breaking, or adding config knobs changes credential availability, security posture, and operator recovery behavior.

options.title: Bounded generic startup policy
options.body: Add source-agnostic bounded startup retry or backoff around SecretRef activation with clear terminal diagnostics, tests, and docs, without hardcoding 1Password behavior.

options.title: Docs and supervisor guidance only
options.body: Keep runtime fail-fast semantics and document launchd/systemd throttling plus external resolver caching, accepting that OpenClaw will not directly reduce provider calls during restart storms.

options.title: Configurable retry/circuit breaker
options.body: Add a new retry or circuit-breaker config surface, accepting higher config, migration, documentation, and upgrade-review cost.

recommendation.title: Bounded generic startup policy
recommendation.body: Add source-agnostic bounded startup retry or backoff around SecretRef activation with clear terminal diagnostics, tests, and docs, without hardcoding 1Password behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest feature-history signal for provider-based external secrets and eager runtime snapshot activation is in joshavant-authored commits.
